quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.quote: Cade Cunningham is getting tired. He is getting exhausted. Where in the F is Jalen Duren, my guy? As much as we love the idea of you, you have been a shart this series. Not even a fart, not a shit, a shart. It is crazy that he is that good and talented and cannot get, you can't get me 14 points? My guy. He is guarding your best player. He is exhausted. My guy, everyone, we should just call him Giannis because he's carrying this team every single game.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights the immense pressure and fatigue on a young star carrying his team in the playoffs, and the underperformance of a key teammate.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.quote: What the Pistons are doing and showing is like, you can't have a one-man show. You can't have a one-man show, right? And what the Cavs are showing is, hey, we can wear you down, work through some of our stuff. Do I agree with everything the Cavs are doing? Hell no. But everyone is coming in, they're starting to really understand how hard it is to not only beat this team, but to be locked in and be connected with their chemistry, with their intensity, starting off the game great and finishing quarters and not making stupid turnovers.
quotes.why_it_matters: Contrasts two team approaches in the playoffs, emphasizing the importance of collective effort and chemistry over individual heroics.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: Now I need you to keep that same energy and apologize to me. Because I told you when you were telling me that Donovan Mitchell needs to take a back seat. I said, 'No the f*** he don't, this is his moment.' What he did in Game 1 and Game 2? Somewhere took a back seat, him and James Harden both trying to force and play team ball, turnovers, not shooting the ball well, wasn't getting to the, all that shit.
quotes.why_it_matters: Recalls a past debate about a star player's approach in critical playoff moments, highlighting the tension between individual brilliance and team play.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: And then all of a sudden, Game 3, Donovan Mitchell had 31. I think on 26 field goal attempts. And then all of a sudden last night he had 43. And they went in great fashion. This ain't the time to be waiting on Evan Mobley. Evan Mobley can find something else to do. Continue to anchor the defense, block some shots, set some screens, do some other shit. Let Donovan Mitchell cook. Mano a mano, let that man go. Donovan Mitchell came into these two home games saying, 'F*** everything else, if we going down, we going down with me, with me shooting this motherf***ing rock.'
quotes.why_it_matters: Advocates for a star player to aggressively take over offensive responsibilities in the playoffs, suggesting other players should focus on complementary roles.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: And guess what, we're seeing a completely different Cavs team. Guess what? Now James Harden all of a sudden his isolation, his looks are getting better because of the aggression of Donovan Mitchell. I'm to the point now where I'm over the point of trying to get Evan Mobley going. Evan Mobley got to find himself in other areas. Same with Jarrett Allen.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains how a star player's offensive aggression can positively influence the entire team's performance and create better opportunities for teammates.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.quote: You know what's crazy? Donovan Mitchell, there's a crazy stat when he shoots, when he's efficient, meaning he has more points than shots, his teams win, I think it's like 78% of the time. That last series, in the first two games, he was wildly inefficient. Last night he went crazy. Can we expect him to get 43 every single night? Maybe. But if you're going to shoot, listen, Donovan Mitchell, if you're going to shoot efficiently, so if you're going to take 25 shots, you got to give me 30 plus points. I think that's efficient. I'm okay with that. He until last night or the time they played at home, he had not shown he can be efficient or inefficient and the Cavs win. So yes, Donovan Mitchell, if you're going to go off, go off, but be efficient about how you do it.
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides a statistical argument for the importance of efficiency in a star player's scoring, directly linking it to team success in the playoffs.
